case_name: Ranip Nagar Palika v Babuji Gabhaji Thakore And Ors
facts: Claim was made by the respondents to the effect that their services were terminated without following the procedure prescribed under Section 25-F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
The Labour Court, Ahmedabad by order dated 9.7.1999 directed re-instatement with continuity of service and 50% back wages.
A brief reference to the factual aspects would suffice.
It was their case that they were employed on regular basis and, therefore, the termination of service is illegal.
The respondents only worked for a few days.
In fact after November, 1993 there was no engagement made as their services were not required.
issues: What is the correct procedure for terminating services under Section 25-F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947?
Who bears the burden of proof in determining whether a workman has completed 240 days of service?
petitioner_arguments: There was no pleading that the respondents had completed 240 days of service.
Their claim in the claim petition was that they had rendered continuous service without indicating any particulars.

All relevant records were produced before the Labour Court which were lightly brushed aside and conclusions were arrived at on conjectures by holding that the claim of the present respondents was to be accepted.
respondent_arguments: After analyzing the factual position in detail the Labour Court and the High Court have arrived at the correct conclusion.
The burden is on the person who claims to have rendered more than 240 days of service to establish it.
court_reasoning: In Range Forest Officer v. S.T. Hadimani (2002 (3) SCC 25), it was held that the burden is on the management to show that there was justification in termination of the service and that the affidavit of the workman was sufficient to prove that he had worked for 240 days in a year.

The Tribunal was not right in placing the onus on the management without first determining on the basis of cogent evidence that the respondent had worked for more than 240 days in the year preceding his termination.
holding: The appeal is allowed and the order passed by the Division Bench of the Gujarat High Court dismissing the Letters Patent Appeal filed by the appellant is set aside.
The respondents will be given an employment on compassionate grounds on the same terms as they were allegedly engaged prior to their termination, within two months from today.
